vuong_son_vuong_huong.y: The mountain chart's timely star sits at the back and the facing chart's timely star at the front — the best formation: the back should be solid and full (hills, tall buildings, walls), the front open, with an entrance or water.
vuong_son_vuong_huong.goi_y: Keep the back closed and solid; the front door and living room should open to the facing side, open and bright.

thuong_son_ha_thuy.y: The mountain's timely star runs to the front and the facing's timely star runs to the back — the old books call this a weaker formation if the setting is ordinary (open in front, solid behind).

song_tinh_dao_huong.y: Both timely stars, mountain and facing, sit at the front: good for money if the front is open yet has something to lean on; watch the people and health side at the back.
song_tinh_dao_huong.goi_y: In front, have both an open yard or path and a row of trees or a solid building some distance away; keep the back stable.

song_tinh_dao_toa.y: Both timely stars sit at the back: good for the people in the house and for stability; money needs an opening at the back.
song_tinh_dao_toa.goi_y: The back should have some open space, a back yard or a side door; keep the front tidy.

the_quai.y: When a house is a 'replacement' facing (the back is more than 3° off the centre of its mountain), its qi is no longer purely one mountain. The Shen school uses the replacement chart: the stars entering the centre of the mountain and facing charts are swapped for 'replacement stars' by a mnemonic, while the direction of flight still follows the yin–yang of the original mountain. The period chart does not change.
the_quai.khau_quyet: Zi, Gui, Jia and Shen go with Tan Lang (1); Ren, Mao, Yi, Wei and Kun with Ju Men (2); Qian, Hai, Chen, Xun, Si and Xu with Wu Qu (6); You, Xin, Chou, Gen and Bing with Po Jun (7); Yin, Wu, Geng and Ding with You Bi (9).
the_quai.luu_y: Schools differ on the threshold (3° or 4.5°), on the direction of flight after the swap and on how star 5 is handled. We follow the Shen school and have no independent source to cross-check yet, so always look at the standard chart too and re-measure with a compass.

luu_nguyet.y: The monthly star changes with the solar terms: the Tiger month begins at Li Chun (Start of Spring), the Rabbit month at Jing Zhe (Awakening of Insects)… In Rat, Horse, Rabbit and Rooster years the Tiger month's centre star is 8; in Dragon, Dog, Ox and Goat years 5; in Tiger, Monkey, Snake and Pig years 2; each month steps back one number.
luu_nguyet.luu_y: The monthly star is only a short-term layer on top of the annual star and the house chart — use it to choose when to break ground, repair or tidy a room; it is not a prediction.
